sections.title: Nonuniqueness of Solutions to 2D Incompressible Euler Equations with Unbounded Vorticity
sections.abstract: Constructs two distinct 2D incompressible Euler solutions with the same compactly supported, mean-zero initial vorticity in every finite $L^p$, using an infinite-scale cascade of quadrupole transitions.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 in the paper constructs two distinct renormalized vorticity solutions with identical initial data, each preserving all finite-$L^p$ vorticity norms, and with velocities in $C([0,\infty);L^2)$.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two-dimensional whole-space incompressible Euler; the common vorticity is compactly supported, mean-zero, and belongs to $\bigcap_{1\le p<\infty}L^p(\mathbb R^2)$.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction is in an unbounded-vorticity class and does not establish nonuniqueness for bounded vorticity or for arbitrary initial data.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete nonuniqueness construction in a central PDE uniqueness question, with compact support and finite-energy velocity; the arXiv comment says a Lean formalisation is forthcoming.

sections.title: Hodge–Riemann relations for nef bundles
sections.abstract: Develops a Lefschetz framework for nef classes and vector bundles and proves Hodge–Riemann relations for specified products of Chern and derived Schur classes under a Hall–Rado-type condition.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract and Theorem 1.4 establish Hodge–Riemann relations for products of top Chern classes and, in suitable bidegrees, derived Schur classes of nef twisted vector bundles, subject to stated Lefschetz/Hall–Rado hypotheses.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact Kähler manifolds, nef twisted vector bundles, and the specified $(m,p,q)$-Lefschetz or Hall–Rado-type conditions; some formal analogues are for projective-bundle modules.
sections.unique_caveat: The positivity conclusions are conditional on these geometric and Lefschetz hypotheses; they are not asserted for arbitrary bundles or classes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed between algebraic geometry and combinatorics; the abstract states a framework, positivity relations, an equivalence for products of nef $(1,1)$-classes, and an extension of the descent lemma.

sections.title: Local Law and Eigenvector Delocalization for Random Lifts
sections.abstract: Proves a quantitative Green-function local law for random lifts of a fixed graph and derives high-probability eigenvector delocalization away from singular energies.
sections.claimed_result: For random $N$-lifts of the stated base graph, the authors obtain entrywise Green-function estimates down to $(\log N)^C/N$ and complete eigenvector delocalization away from the universal-cover spectrum’s singular energies.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The base is a fixed finite connected simple graph of minimum degree at least three; the estimates hold with high probability and exclude singular energies by a fixed positive margin.
sections.unique_caveat: The singular energies are explicitly excluded, and the logarithmic exponent and constants are not specified in the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A precise quantitative result spanning probability, mathematical physics, combinatorics, and spectral theory; it reaches spectral scales $(\log N)^C/N$ and yields a sup-norm eigenvector bound.

sections.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP I: The shock region
sections.abstract: Interprets the Bryc polynomial in the open ASEP stationary-measure representation through a birth–death-type chain and obtains sharp total-variation approximations in the shock region’s high- and low-density phases.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract gives a probabilistic birth–death-chain interpretation of the Bryc polynomial and sharp total-variation approximation by Bernoulli product measures in the shock region, with moderate-deviation applications.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Open ASEP on a finite one-dimensional lattice, under the paper’s boundary-rate/Liggett conditions and in the high- or low-density shock phases.
sections.unique_caveat: This installment addresses the shock region; its approximation statements are phase- and parameter-dependent and are not a single approximation for all stationary regimes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: First of a coordinated three-paper treatment of distinct open-ASEP regimes; cross-listed in probability and mathematical physics. Semantic Scholar currently lists 1 citation, including 1 influential citation, and 45 references; these are current totals, not period gains.

sections.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP III: The fan region
sections.abstract: Establishes total-variation approximations for open-ASEP configurations in the fan region by random-walk excursions, meanders, or Bernoulli product configurations, depending on phase.
sections.claimed_result: In the maximal-current phase and its fan-region boundaries, occupation variables are approximated by configurations built from lazy-walk excursions/meanders; in high- and low-density phases, Bernoulli product approximations have exponentially decaying errors away from the relevant boundary.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Open ASEP in the fan region, with general boundary rates; separate claims apply to the maximal-current, boundary, and high-/low-density phases.
sections.unique_caveat: The approximation changes with the phase and location; it does not cover arbitrary regimes or claim identical fluctuation laws throughout the phase diagram.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Completes a three-paper, regime-based open-ASEP program and supplies discrete fluctuation counterparts plus moderate-deviation estimates. Semantic Scholar currently lists 2 citations and 0 influential citations; these are current totals, not period gains.

sections.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP II: The coexistence line
sections.abstract: On the open ASEP coexistence line, identifies the shock location and approximates its distribution by a uniform lattice law, with conditional product-measure approximations away from the shock.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that the shock location’s law is close in total variation to the uniform lattice law and, conditional on that location, the occupation variables away from the shock are close to Bernoulli product measures with different left/right densities.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The open ASEP on the coexistence line, using the two-layer representation and birth–death-chain characterization developed in Part I.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is specific to the coexistence line and relies on the representation established in the companion work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Adds an explicit shock-location observable and optimal total-variation bounds within the same three-part probability/statistical-physics series. Semantic Scholar currently lists 2 citations and 0 influential citations; these are current totals, not period gains.

sections.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
sections.abstract: Proves an optimal cubic bound for threefold additive energy on lattice circles and a uniform weak-$L^6$ estimate for normalized square-torus eigenfunctions, with further nodal and convergence applications.
sections.claimed_result: For $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb Z^2:|z|^2=n\}$, the authors prove $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$ and a uniform weak-$L^6$ bound, implying uniform $L^p$ bounds for $1\le p<6$.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Lattice points on circles and $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions of the square torus; the weak endpoint is $p=6$.
sections.unique_caveat: The endpoint claim is weak-$L^6$, not a strong-$L^6$ estimate.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract identifies the additive-energy bound as optimal and links it to a weak-$L^6$ eigenfunction estimate; it is cross-listed across four mathematical areas.

sections.title: Enumeration of zero-sum subsequences: A proof of Bialostocki-Lotspeich conjecture
sections.abstract: Proves the 1992 Bialostocki–Lotspeich lower bound for the number of $n$-element zero-sum subsequences in a sequence over the cyclic group of order $n$.
sections.claimed_result: For a sequence $S$ over $C_n$, the authors prove $\mathsf N_0^n(S)\ge\binom{\lfloor |S|/2\rfloor}{n}+\binom{\lceil |S|/2\rceil}{n}$, the conjectured bound.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite sequences with repetitions allowed in the cyclic group $C_n$, for $n\ge2$; the counted subsequences have exactly $n$ terms.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated theorem concerns cyclic groups of order equal to the subsequence length; it does not by itself establish the analogous bound for arbitrary finite abelian groups.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a complete proof of a named conjecture, with a natural bridge between additive combinatorics and number theory.

sections.title: High-dimensional critical percolation and critical Branching random walks are intersection equivalent
sections.abstract: Shows that, in dimensions above six under a standard two-point/Green-function comparability assumption, distant finite sets are hit with comparable probabilities by a critical percolation cluster and a critical branching random walk.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract proves two-sided comparison up to positive multiplicative constants of the hit probabilities for any finite set sufficiently far from the origin relative to its diameter.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Critical percolation and critical branching random walk on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d>6$, assuming their two-point function and the Green function have the same order.
sections.unique_caveat: The comparison is only established in the stated high-dimensional regime and for sets satisfying the far-from-origin versus diameter condition.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: States a direct comparison between two canonical critical random structures and provides an explicit approximate-last-passage/equilibrium-measure method.

sections.title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities
sections.abstract: Proves a functional inequality stronger than Poincaré for uniformly log-concave measures and uses it to give sharp stability of Brenier potentials under target-measure variation.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract’s inequality controls the variance of differences of convex functions and yields a sharp stability bound for Brenier potentials; its Gaussian application recovers equivalence of Bures–Wasserstein and Frobenius distances between positive-semidefinite matrix square roots.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A fixed uniformly log-concave source measure and changes in the target measure; the proof uses linearization of the quadratic-transport Monge–Ampère equation.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated stability theory assumes uniform log-concavity of the source and does not cover arbitrary source measures.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Connects optimal transport, functional inequalities, and metric geometry, and gives a Gaussian-matrix application; it is cross-listed in four math subjects.

sections.title: The Assouad Dimension of Graphs: An Affirmative Answer to Fraser's Question
sections.abstract: Studies Assouad dimensions of graphs of continuous functions, deriving level-set bounds and a partial positive answer to questions of Fraser and Yu, with examples including Weierstrass- and Takagi-type functions.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract proves a lower bound for the Assouad dimension of graphs of count-Hölder continuous functions in terms of the supremum of upper box dimensions of level sets, and shows that this lower bound is sharp in the stated sense.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Graphs of continuous functions on a compact interval under the paper’s count-Hölder hypotheses; the paper also treats specified Weierstrass-type and self-affine examples.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors describe their answer to Fraser’s question as partial, not a complete resolution of every formulation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Addresses named dimension questions and links fractal geometry of function graphs to level-set and box-dimension estimates; it has three math-subfield listings.
